evidence: Receiving online DO2 (available through 52.0 h): values 7.9-14.8 mg/L, minimum in most recent window ~7.88 mg/L at ~52 h — large margin over the 2 mg/L limit.
Receiving delayed product assays: P = 0.0 (59 h), 0.04 (119 h), 1.17 (179 h), 3.30 (239 h) g/L — accelerating production consistent with source batches (3.0-5.5 g/L at same assay times).
Source batch DO2 trajectories are structurally similar to the receiving train, supporting normal-behavior inference with no evidence of oxygen limitation.
Allowed action semantics: keep = (1.0, 1.0) — no feed or air change; zero risk of constraint violation or product-mass loss from the action itself.
args.rationale: Receiving fermentation is healthy and within limits. Online DO2 has never approached the 2 mg/L hard constraint: values range ~7.9-14.8 mg/L, with the most recent 30 h window (t≈230-259 h sensor timestamps, all available by the 52 h decision clock) holding between 7.88 and 9.02 mg/L and declining only ~0.03 mg/L/h. Delayed product assays show accelerating growth (0.0 at 59 h, 0.04 at 119 h, 1.17 at 179 h, 3.30 g/L at 239 h), consistent with the three source batches (which reached 6.4-8.4 g/L). Feed reduction or air changes would sacrifice product mass or add unnecessary actuation risk with no offsetting benefit; a stop would zero counted production. KEEP is the supported feasible plan that retains full product mass with a large DO margin (~4x the limit).
args.uncertainty: Key gaps: hidden receiving parameters and future states are unavailable; the DO2 decline rate (~0.03 mg/L/h) extrapolated still leaves months of margin, but an unmodeled demand spike could steepen the trend. Source and receiving processes differ, so source trajectories are only weak evidence of receiving behavior. If DO2 later falls below ~4 mg/L, feed reduction should be reconsidered; no current evidence supports that.
